evidence: "MEASURED — an instrumented run under the Chapter 14 protocol; used only where the book reports a benchmark it actually ran, never for a planning screen. ANALYTICAL — arithmetic on stated inputs … HYPOTHESIS — reasoned but not yet validated … ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example … The four registers above are not one axis: MEASURED, ANALYTICAL and HYPOTHESIS name what was done to a number, whereas [ILLUSTRATIVE] names where it came from — so a single claim can be both ILLUSTRATIVE and ANALYTICAL."
issue: Internal contradiction in the evidence-panel definition. The panel opens by presenting 'four registers' as a unified set, then states 'The four registers above are not one axis' — denying they form one axis while having just framed them as four parallel registers. Worse, MEASURED is listed as a register in this panel, but the Preface axis note (p.19) says 'measurement status therefore uses ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED or UNMEASURED' — i.e., MEASURED is a measurement-status value on Axis 3, not a register (the registers are Axis 1 provenance + Axis 2 epistemic status). The panel never reconciles MEASURED's dual role. Separately, ANALYTICAL appears both as one of the four 'registers' and as a measurement status on Axis 3, with no statement of whether these are the same item or two uses of one word. A reader cannot tell from this panel alone how to apply the labels correctly.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the evidence-panel opening to state plainly that two label axes (provenance, epistemic status) plus an optional measurement-status axis are used, drop the 'four registers' framing (or define exactly which axis each of the four belongs to), and add one sentence clarifying whether MEASURED and ANALYTICAL as used in the panel are the same items as the Axis-3 measurement statuses or distinct categories.

evidence: Contents (p.6–7) lists 'List of Figures . . . iv' as the only front-matter list; no 'List of Tables' entry appears. Tables in the body include (non-exhaustive) Table 1-1 (p.33), Table 2-1 (p.39), Table 2-2 (p.43), Table 3-1 (p.60), Table 3-2 (p.61), Table 3-3 (p.72), Table 4-1 (p.78), Table 4-2 (p.91), Table 5-1 (p.115), Table 5-2 (p.117), Table 6-1 (p.137), Table 7-1 (p.147), Table 7-2 (p.154), Table 7-3 (p.165), Table 8-1 (p.180).
issue: The front matter provides a 'List of Figures' (pp.8–10) but no corresponding 'List of Tables', despite at least fifteen numbered tables that readers and cross-references rely on (e.g., 'Table 4-2' is cited dozens of times across chapters as the canonical provenance ledger). The omission makes it impossible to locate a table by number without scanning the whole book, and it is inconsistent with the front-matter convention established by the figure list.
fix_instruction: Add a 'List of Tables' after the List of Figures (and a Contents entry for it), listing every Table N-M with its caption and printed page number.

evidence: Figure 1 caption: "Two loops are drawn: the inner (green, left) returns a failed benchmark or TCO validation from 'Validate & Defend' to 'Design & size'; the outer (red, right) returns from 'Commit' to 'Understand' when a requirements revision is needed." In-figure text (rendered page): "iterate", "re-derive" appear as edge labels; stage category labels "understand / define / size / justify / decide" also appear in the figure.
issue: Two defects in one caption. (1) The caption identifies the two loops only by color ('green', 'red') and position ('left', 'right'), but the book's own stated convention (Ch. 7 intro, p.143: 'Color is not semantic anywhere in this chapter's figures'; and the general figure convention, p.42: 'Color is figure-local decoration') warns readers not to rely on color — in a grayscale print or photocopy the two loops become indistinguishable. (2) The caption does not mention the in-figure edge labels 'iterate' and 're-derive' or the four stage-category labels (understand, define, size, justify, decide) that appear in the figure, so the caption under-describes what the figure shows and a reader cannot tell from the caption alone what those words mean.
fix_instruction: Identify the loops by their edge labels and stage endpoints (e.g., 'the inner loop, labelled iterate …; the outer loop, labelled re-derive …') rather than by color/position alone, and add one clause naming the stage-category labels visible in the figure.

evidence: "Every quantitative value here is one of three kinds: a dated measurement, a figure derived from cited inputs, or is explicitly identified as an illustrative assumption (see the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter for the full evidence taxonomy)."
issue: The copyright page states quantitative values come in 'three kinds', but the Preface evidence panel (p.18) presents 'four registers' (MEASURED, ANALYTICAL, ILLUSTRATIVE, HYPOTHESIS) and the Preface axis definitions (pp.19) add a fifth epistemic state (UNRESOLVED) plus a third axis of measurement statuses (ANALYTICAL / SCENARIO-DERIVED / MODELED / MEASURED / UNMEASURED). The 'three kinds' summary is a simplification of a system the Preface itself describes as multi-axis; a careful reader comparing the two passages sees different counts (3 vs 4 vs 6+) for the same taxonomy. The mismatch is small but it is the very kind of internal inconsistency the book's evidence discipline is meant to prevent.
fix_instruction: Either change 'three kinds' to match the Preface's actual taxonomy (e.g., 'three provenance/status categories, with additional measurement-status labels defined in …') or add a parenthetical noting the copyright-page list is a simplified summary and the Preface/Sources chapter defines the full label set.

evidence: "A single token can be a whole word (handbook), a common subword (hand), a single character, a short punctuation+space pair, or in worst cases a single byte (a fragment of a character)." and §1.1.1: "the 'one token ≈ 4 characters' rule of thumb is for rough estimation of general-English prose, never a law" [2°][FACT].
issue: The [2°][FACT] label on the '4 characters ≈ 1 token' rule of thumb (p.27) claims a reputable second-hand source states it as fact, but no source is named inline or in a footnote for this specific claim anywhere in Chapter 1 (the only [2°][FACT] nearby is about high-frequency English words rendering as single tokens, which is a different claim). A [2°][FACT] label without a traceable source is a provenance gap under the book's own rule that 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair' and that [2°] means 'reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark' — the source must be identifiable.
fix_instruction: Either cite the specific textbook/survey that states the ~4-chars-per-token heuristic (add an [S#] or footnote), or downgrade the label to [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] / [HYPOTHESIS] since the heuristic is a rough rule rather than a sourced fact.

evidence: Table 6-1 appears after the text in §6.3.3 but no sentence in §6.3 introduces or cites it (the preceding paragraph ends with '…see Ch 8 for the underlying intensity/roofline arithmetic that shows why these regimes occur.'), and the table's caption line reads 'Table 6-1 — Detecting the bottleneck regime from resource telemetry' with no 'see Table 6-1' pointer anywhere in the section body.
issue: Table 6-1 is introduced without a forward reference in the running text. The book's own cross-reference convention (Preface, p.19) establishes explicit references ('§ N.M', 'Table N-M'), and every other table in the visible pages is either introduced in prose or cited by number (e.g., 'Table 4-2' is cited throughout, 'Table 7-1' is named in §7.3). Table 6-1 simply appears after a paragraph with no textual pointer, so a reader scanning for 'Table 6-1' in the section text will not find it. This is a minor but real navigability gap.
fix_instruction: Add a one-line pointer before or after the table, e.g., 'Table 6-1 summarizes the regime-detection arithmetic for both phases.'
